pages.title: Fix and Flip
pages.summary: Find distressed properties with room for margin.
pages.headline: Fix and Flip: Buy the Margin, Not the House.
pages.lede: A flip is made or lost at purchase. The goal is to find sellers who value speed and certainty over top dollar, and to know your numbers before you make the offer.
pages.intro: Most flippers compete for the same listed properties and the same wholesale emails. The deals with real margin tend to come from conversations with owners before a property ever hits the market. That takes a steady pipeline of the right sellers, and the discipline to run the numbers on every one.

sections.title: Target the right distress
sections.text: Good flip candidates usually combine a dated or damaged property with an owner who needs to move on. We build lists around those signals so callers spend their time on owners who can say yes.

sections.title: Qualify before you drive out
sections.text: Every lead comes back with full MTCP notes: the seller's Motivation, Timeline, property Condition and Price expectations. You see the repair picture and the seller's flexibility before you spend an afternoon on a walkthrough.

sections.title: Know your maximum offer
sections.text: Work backward from the after-repair value. A common rule of thumb starts around 70% of ARV minus repairs, then adjusts for your market, holding costs and target profit. Comps and repair estimates based on square footage keep every offer grounded in numbers, not hope.

pages.ctaText: Trained callers who find and qualify distressed sellers for you.

pages.title: Buy and Hold
pages.summary: Off-market rentals from owners ready to sell.
pages.headline: Buy and Hold: Build the Portfolio Off-Market.
pages.lede: Rental portfolios grow fastest when you can buy below retail. Off-market sellers, especially tired landlords, often care more about an easy exit than the last dollar.
pages.intro: Long-term holds live or die on purchase price and cash flow. Buying on the MLS means competing with every other investor for the same thin margins. Talking directly to owners lets you find properties that cash flow from day one, or that are worth renovating and refinancing.

sections.title: Find the tired landlord
sections.text: Owners who are worn out by tenants, repairs or distance are some of the most motivated sellers in any market. We target them directly.
points: Properties with code or maintenance issues

sections.title: Ask the questions that matter for a hold
sections.text: Beyond MTCP, callers capture what a rental buyer needs to know: current occupancy, rent and lease terms, and the condition of major systems. That makes it fast to judge cash flow before you make an offer.

sections.title: Plan the exit before you buy
sections.text: Whether you keep it as is or renovate, refinance and repeat, the numbers have to work at purchase. Run comps and rent estimates on every qualified lead so you only chase the properties that fit your criteria.

pages.ctaText: Off-market conversations with owners who are ready to sell.

pages.title: Seller Finance
pages.summary: Spot owners open to terms instead of cash.
pages.headline: Seller Finance: When the Answer Is Terms, Not Price.
pages.lede: Some sellers will never accept a cash discount but will gladly take a fair price paid over time. Recognizing them on the first call opens deals your competitors pass on.
pages.intro: Seller financing lets you buy without a bank loan, with the owner carrying the note. It works best for owners who own free and clear or have high equity, and who value monthly income or a smoother tax picture over a lump sum. The skill is spotting these sellers early and knowing when to bring terms up.

sections.title: Who says yes to terms
sections.text: Terms conversations usually start with owners who don't need the cash right away.
points: Retiring landlords who want monthly income
Sellers whose price is above what a cash buyer will pay
Properties that are hard to finance traditionally

sections.title: Listen for the signals
sections.text: Callers are trained to notice when price is the sticking point but timeline isn't. Phrases like "I'm not in a rush" or "I don't need it all at once" are a cue to explore terms instead of pushing a lower number.

sections.title: Structure with professionals
sections.text: Interest rate, down payment, term and balloon all shape whether a deal works for both sides. Seller-financed deals involve lending and disclosure rules that vary by state, so close them with a real estate attorney or title company.

pages.disclaimer: This page is general information, not legal, tax or financial advice. Speak with a licensed attorney before structuring a seller-financed purchase.
pages.ctaText: Callers trained to spot terms opportunities on the first conversation.

pages.title: Seller Listing Opportunities
pages.headline: Seller Listing Opportunities: More Conversations, More Appointments.
pages.lede: Listings come from conversations with homeowners who need to sell. The hard part is having enough of them, consistently, without spending your whole day on the phone.
pages.intro: Expired listings, for-sale-by-owner sellers and homeowners facing foreclosure are some of the clearest signs that someone needs help selling. Each needs a different conversation, and all of them need persistent, professional follow-up. Our callers handle the dialing and qualifying so you can spend your time at the listing appointment.

sections.title: Work the lists that signal a move
sections.text: Each list has its own reason to call and its own opening.

sections.title: Qualify, then book
sections.text: Callers confirm the seller's motivation, timeline, property condition and price expectations, then book qualified sellers straight onto your calendar with notes, so you walk in knowing what matters to them.

sections.title: Follow up until the timing is right
sections.text: Many sellers aren't ready on the first call. A consistent follow-up rhythm keeps you in the conversation until they are. All calling is screened against Do Not Call lists and follows our compliance procedures.

pages.ctaText: Callers who work your seller lists and fill your calendar.

pages.title: Buyer Opportunities
pages.summary: Fast follow-up that turns inquiries into showings.
pages.headline: Buyer Opportunities: Speed Wins the Showing.
pages.lede: Buyer inquiries go cold fast. The agent who responds first and keeps following up is usually the one who gets the showing.
pages.intro: Online inquiries, open-house sign-ins and past leads in your CRM are all buyers who raised a hand at some point. Most agents can't call every one quickly or keep following up for months. A dedicated VA can, so more of those leads become conversations, showings and closings.

sections.title: Respond while the lead is warm
sections.text: Fast first contact on new inquiries, with a short qualification on timeline, financing and what the buyer is looking for, then a hand-off to you when they're ready to see homes.

sections.title: Revive the leads you already have
sections.text: Your CRM likely holds buyers who went quiet. Systematic re-engagement finds the ones whose timeline has arrived.

sections.title: Keep the pipeline organized
sections.text: Every conversation is logged in your CRM with notes and next steps, so nothing falls through the cracks between showings.

pages.ctaTitle: Never let a buyer go cold
pages.ctaText: A trained VA who follows up on every inquiry.

pages.title: Listing Marketing Support
pages.summary: Video, social posts and listing admin, handled.
pages.headline: Listing Marketing Support: Win the Listing, Then Market It Well.
pages.lede: Sellers choose agents who market their home well. Listing video, social posts and clean MLS data take hours that most agents would rather spend with clients.
pages.intro: Great listing marketing is consistent, fast and accurate. Delegating the production work keeps every listing looking professional without pulling you away from appointments and negotiations.

sections.title: Listing video and social content
sections.text: Turn your footage and photos into short listing videos and social posts, by request, so every listing gets the same quality of promotion.

sections.title: Listing admin, done right
sections.text: Delegate the repetitive work while you stay in control of what goes live.
points: MLS photo uploads and data entry
Listing descriptions written to fair housing guidelines

sections.title: Stay visible between listings
sections.text: Regular posts and simple market updates keep you in front of past clients and your sphere, the people most likely to refer your next listing.

pages.ctaText: A trained VA for listing content and admin, by request.

pages.title: How We Operate
pages.summary: Onboarding, daily QA, reporting and management.
pages.headline: How We Operate: A Managed Team, Not Just a Caller.
pages.lede: Every VoloLeads campaign runs on the same routine: a clear setup, daily quality checks and reporting you can read in minutes.
pages.intro: Hiring a caller is easy. Keeping one productive, coached and accountable every day is the hard part. That management layer is what you get with VoloLeads: a trained caller, a VA manager who oversees them, and a daily rhythm of calling, review and reporting.

sections.title: Setup before the first dial
sections.text: We start with a 30-minute strategy call about your markets and goals. After checkout we collect access, agree your lead criteria and calling hours, and set up scripts and routing. Calling usually starts within 48–72 hours of completed onboarding.

sections.title: A daily rhythm of calling and QA
sections.text: Callers work set calling blocks on your campaign. Their VA manager reviews calls every day, coaches on what to improve and keeps dispositions clean.
points: An underperforming caller is replaced with a new VA

sections.title: Reporting you can act on
sections.text: You get a daily report on dials, conversations and leads, and a monthly report with VA timesheets, campaign KPIs, outbound and inbound call history, and the smart lists prepared for your campaign.

pages.title: TCPA Compliance
pages.summary: DNC screening, opt-outs and how our callers stay compliant.
pages.headline: TCPA and Calling Compliance: How Our Callers Work.
pages.lede: Cold calling property owners comes with real rules. Our procedures are built around them, from the list we dial to how a call ends.
pages.intro: The Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA), Do Not Call rules and state calling laws shape how outbound campaigns must run. Our approach combines daily Do Not Call screening, trained human callers, respectful conversations, opt-out handling and campaign reporting. The full detail is in our Compliance Policy.

sections.title: Screened lists, every day
sections.text: Contacts come from property-data and skip-tracing providers such as XLeads, DealMachine and PropStream. Skip tracing finds contact details; it does not give permission to call.
points: Screened against national and applicable state Do Not Call lists before a list is exported
DNC checks refreshed daily before each calling session
Contacts marked Do Not Contact or Not Interested are excluded
Calling hours set per market from written rules

sections.title: Human callers, honest introductions
sections.text: Outbound calls are made by trained human VAs through third-party dialers, with no AI-generated or prerecorded voices. Callers say they are calling on behalf of a partner interested in buying in the area, never claim to be the buyer, and do not pressure or argue with owners who decline.

sections.title: Respecting requests to stop
sections.text: If an owner is not interested, the call ends respectfully and the contact is marked Not Interested. A request to stop contact is marked Do Not Contact and excluded from future lists. For SMS, clients supply documented opt-in consent and registration such as A2P 10DLC, and STOP replies end messaging immediately.

pages.disclaimer: This page summarises our procedures and is not legal advice. Our procedures reduce risk but cannot guarantee a campaign will never receive a complaint or claim, and VoloLeads does not offer contractual indemnification. Read the full Compliance Policy and Terms of Service before purchasing.
pages.ctaText: Talk through your markets and requirements on a strategy call.

pages.title: AI Workflows
pages.summary: Where AI helps, and where people stay in charge.
pages.headline: AI Workflows: Automation Around the Call, Not Instead of It.
pages.lede: We use AI where it saves time without losing judgment: routing, reporting, follow-up and inbound coverage. Outbound seller calls stay human.
pages.intro: Most of the busywork in an acquisitions operation happens around the call: moving data between tools, logging notes, chasing replies and pulling reports. AI connectors that plug into your CRM and dialer handle that work, so your callers and your team spend their time on conversations.

sections.title: Connected to your CRM and dialer
sections.text: AI connectors move data between the tools you already use and keep records tidy.

sections.title: SMS and inbound voice coverage
sections.text: On the Scale plan, AI automation handles SMS replies and acts as a voice receptionist for inbound calls, so a seller calling back is answered instead of reaching voicemail. SMS runs only on client-supplied, consented contacts, and STOP replies end messaging immediately.

sections.title: People stay in charge
sections.text: Outbound seller calls are made by trained human VAs, never AI or prerecorded voices. AI workflows are set up and reviewed by our team and built around your process; we only connect the tools your campaign actually uses.

pages.ctaText: Map the AI workflows that fit your stack on a strategy call.
